sources.name: playwright
sources.why: The broadest suite of automation edge cases. Its Firefox and WebKit results come from Playwright's patched builds, so its per-browser annotations say little about stock browsers.

sources.name: puppeteer
sources.why: Drives Firefox over WebDriver BiDi, as Strider does, and keeps a ledger of expected failures per browser and protocol with their Bugzilla links. Also CDP target, out-of-process iframe, and worker behavior.

sources.name: cypress
sources.why: Waiting: its driver tests pin down retry-ability and actionability (covered, detached, animating, disabled, or scrolled away) with assertions on how long and how often a command retries, which is what an optimal wait has to get right.

sources.name: foldkit-examples
sources.why: Real apps: 120 Playwright tests over 33 example applications, a ready-made suite of an app's own end-to-end tests to run with Strider.

sources.name: wpt-accessibility
sources.why: Role and accessible-name computation, which getByRole and snapshots depend on. Playwright's role-utils.spec.ts runs some of these.

sources.name: wpt-input
sources.why: Event sequences real input must produce (pointer, mouse, focus, and key), written against testdriver's actions, which a port can drive with Strider's input instead.

sources.name: wpt-webdriver-bidi
sources.why: Tests the browser, not the client: evidence for whether an oddity is a Firefox or Safari bug, and for the BiDi capability tables. Not ported to run; read when a Firefox finding needs its cause.

sources.name: testing-library
sources.why: What users expect getByRole, getByLabelText, and getByText to match, from the library most of them learned queries from.

sources.name: chromedp
sources.why: A CDP client in Go: its tests cover target attachment, out-of-process iframes, and frame lifecycles from the protocol's side.
